title: Monetary-policy expectation estimates vary with the design used to measure the announcement response
source_unit: US household respondent in a two-wave survey comparison around a Federal Reserve announcement

observations.period: September 2025 Federal Reserve rate-cut announcement; two-wave survey

denominator.unit: NBER paper comparison of three survey designs; design-specific respondent counts are not stated on the metadata page

designs_compared.value: randomized hypothetical scenarios, randomized information provision, and surveys immediately before and after an actual announcement

direction_of_expectation_change.value: rate cuts are associated with lower expected inflation and unemployment and stronger expected economic activity

vignette_vs_rct_event_estimates.value: vignette estimates are substantially larger than average randomized-information and event-study estimates

observations.method: NBER Working Paper 35090 comparison of hypothetical, randomized-information, and actual-announcement event-study designs embedded in a two-wave survey.
observations.uncertainty: The full-paper numerical estimates are recorded in a separate observation below; the designs identify different reduced-form objects and do not estimate a structural exogenous monetary-policy shock or general-equilibrium effect.
observations.subgroup: Expectation revisions vary with respondent-specific policy surprises; detailed prior-knowledge and exposure splits are recorded below.
observations.counterinterpretation: A hypothetical vignette can amplify stated responses relative to an information treatment or real announcement because it removes awareness, salience, comprehension, or concurrent-news constraints; a shared direction does not imply equal behavioral magnitude.

denominator.unit: design-specific RCT and pre/post comparison subsets; exact counts not stated on the metadata page

new_information_rct_alignment.value: differences between the RCT and event-study estimates shrink among RCT respondents for whom the decision was new information

announcement_awareness_condition.value: pre/post expectation revisions are compared among respondents who knew about the decision

policy_surprise_gradient.value: expectation revisions vary systematically with respondent-specific policy surprises

observations.method: Comparative analysis of treatment-information status, announcement awareness, and respondent-specific policy surprises across the three survey designs.
observations.uncertainty: The surprise and awareness comparisons are not interchangeable population treatment effects; event-study exposure is not randomized and the expectation measures do not establish realized spending, borrowing, saving, or trust.
observations.subgroup: Respondents classified by whether the policy decision was new information, whether they knew about the announcement, and the size or direction of their policy surprise.
observations.counterinterpretation: Conditioning on awareness or new information can select respondents with different financial literacy, media exposure, prior beliefs, or interest in the Federal Reserve; the design comparison is not automatically a population treatment effect.

observations.period: September 2025 FOMC meeting; full-paper design and sample audit

denominator.unit: pooled Wave 1/Wave 2 event-study observations; balanced panel has 1,308 recontacted respondents

fomc_action.value: 25 basis point federal-funds-rate cut on September 17, 2025

vignette_sample.unit: valid one-year-inflation vignette observations; other outcome counts vary slightly

rct_sample.unit: recontacted respondents in randomized information-treatment analysis

event_study_sample.value: 6,968 pooled cross-section observations and 1,308 balanced-panel respondents

observations.method: Two-wave survey around the September 2025 FOMC meeting combining randomized hypothetical scenarios, randomized information treatment, repeated cross-section, balanced-panel, respondent-fixed-effect, and exposure/perception comparisons; robust standard errors reported.
observations.uncertainty: The paper is a working paper and the designs identify different reduced-form responses to communicated or observed policy actions, not a structural exogenous monetary-policy shock or general-equilibrium effect. Event-study exposure is not randomized, and the analysis is based on survey expectations rather than realized household financial behavior.
observations.subgroup: RCT prior knowledge: 43% previously unaware and 57% previously aware; event-study balanced-panel exposure: about 85% reported hearing/substantive belief, with 1,108 exposed and 200 unexposed; among exposed, 751 correctly perceived the cut and 357 did not.
observations.counterinterpretation: The rate decision can signal the Federal Reserve's information about inflation or labor-market weakness, not only change borrowing conditions. The event study also includes the statement, press conference, media reactions, and other concurrent news.

observations.period: September 2025 FOMC meeting; cross-design one-year expectation estimates

denominator.unit: design-specific regression estimates; denominators are reported in the full-paper audit observation

event_full_1y_inflation.unit: percentage points; robust SE 0.081; repeated cross-section

observations.method: Cross-design estimates from the paper's vignette, randomized information-treatment, and event-study specifications with baseline expectation and demographic controls where specified; robust standard errors in parentheses.
observations.uncertainty: The estimates are not interchangeable average treatment effects. Vignette exposure is universal and hypothetical; RCT treatment communicates a realized decision and is attenuated by prior knowledge; event-study exposure is naturally occurring and includes concurrent announcement information. None estimates realized spending, debt, saving, or portfolio changes.
observations.subgroup: One-year inflation expectation estimates split by RCT prior knowledge and event-study announcement exposure/correct perception.
observations.counterinterpretation: The negative inflation-expectation response to a rate cut differs from a conventional demand-channel prediction and may reflect respondents inferring weaker inflation or labor-market conditions from the central bank's action.

observations.period: Pre-trial registration published September 3, 2025; planned study window September 10, 2025-September 30, 2026

denominator.unit: planned Wave 1 online-survey respondents; registry also planned approximately 2,100 Wave 2 respondents

planned_wave1_arm_size.unit: approximately planned respondents per Wave 1 group

planned_wave2_arm_size.unit: approximately planned respondents per Wave 2 group

primary_outcome.value: updating of macroeconomic expectations under hypothetical versus factual policy information

observations.method: AEA RCT Registry pre-trial registration AEARCTR-0016642; registration page reports planned sample sizes, individual randomization, intervention dates, and primary outcome family.
observations.uncertainty: The registry is a planned-design artifact, not evidence that the planned sample, arm sizes, or intervention window were fully realized. The public page reports limited experimental-design detail and states that some information is unavailable.
observations.subgroup: Planned Wave 1 hypothetical/control groups and Wave 2 information/control groups; registration does not provide the final analytic subgroup counts used in the paper.
observations.counterinterpretation: A final sample larger or smaller than the plan can reflect recontact, eligibility, exclusions, or recruitment changes; planned and analyzed denominators must not be silently substituted for one another.

boundary: This record promotes the author-hosted August 2026 full-paper estimates and design audit while preserving the working-paper, survey-expectation, reduced-form, exposure, and no-realized-action boundaries. It does not establish a structural monetary-policy shock, general-equilibrium effect, household spending/debt response, trust change, or political consequence.
